response.justification: Broad, senior-level engineer with 15+ years across web, backend, embedded and infrastructure, including genuinely relevant high-throughput distributed systems work at Sociomantic/dunnhumby (micro-services handling millions of HTTP requests per second, async I/O, fibers, caching) and current Staff-level work at re:cinq on AI-agent infrastructure, MCP code generators and agentic workflow tooling — which directly matches the AI-native engineering mindset the role treats as baseline. The main gap is the explicit must-have: Python is absent from the skills list and every role description, while the deepest systems work is in DLang and the recent five years are mostly TypeScript/Node product work. Evidence of technical strategy at scale, cross-functional stakeholder management, and on-call/operational ownership is also thin relative to a Staff bar. Worth an interview to probe Python depth and current distributed-systems currency, but not a clear yes on paper.
strengths: Proven high-throughput, low-latency distributed systems experience (millions of req/sec)
Hands-on agentic/AI tooling work: MCP code generators and agent frameworks
Strong engineering-craft culture: TDD, CI/CD, trunk-based, teaching and OSS leadership
concerns: No Python evidence anywhere in the resume despite it being a must-have
Limited demonstrated technical-strategy, stakeholder-management, or on-call ownership at Staff scale
Deep distributed-systems work is ~6 years old; recent roles skew to product/full-stack TypeScript
